markdown_report:
The next experiment should complete an auditable recent-cutoff comparison before adding architecture. The supplied snapshots already identify a `recent10` treatment; they do not establish improvement over a matched uniform control.

Three starting-point insights guide this choice. First, recent10 changes probabilities only for histories longer than twelve events, approximately 16–28% of eligible users. Actual changed terminal selections also exclude endpoint draws. Second, Industrial and Electronics retain weak-margin rates of 10.93% and 10.25%. These training probes motivate discrimination checks, not claims about held-out ranking. Third, snapshots record equal branch counts while definitions describe Bernoulli(0.75) allocation. Definitions must match executed training before attributing allocation effects.

Three literature insights clarify the contribution. BERT4Rec [1] explicitly includes last-item-only training alongside random masking. It does not establish arbitrary-prefix truncation as its augmentation policy. RSS [2] establishes recency-biased target selection, removing targets while retaining subsequent interactions. Strict-prefix terminal masking differs in context and objective, but recency sampling itself is established. Sequential Masked Modeling [3] motivates studying masking and windows. Its reported gains do not validate this cutoff mixture.

The framework separates three directions: **target exposure** through sampling, **temporal relevance** through attention, and **semantic specificity** through jointly trained text. Sampling preserves inference; temporal and semantic changes require synchronized predictor updates. Evaluate them separately.

Scores use O/F/U/M/D: originality, future potential, user alignment, model alignment and implementation difficulty; higher D means harder. Each cell gives a positive and negative assessment.

| Idea | O | F | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Audited cutoff comparison [1–3] | 2: precise adaptation; established sampling principle | 6: interpretable foundation; limited coverage | 6: targets staleness/specificity; cannot infer needs | 5: tests weak-tail discrimination; probe mismatch | 4: sampler unchanged at inference; audit requires care |
| Elapsed-time attention [4] | 4: BERT adaptation; established mechanism | 7: flexible relevance; gaps ambiguous | 7: may reduce staleness; no compatibility evidence | 5: contextual discrimination; no causal diagnosis | 6: small bias module; timestamp/predictor changes |
| Joint title/description encoder [5] | 4: constrained combination; established semantics | 7: shares descriptive evidence; sparse text | 6: specific descriptors; similarity may reinforce redundancy | 5: item sharing; weak margins may persist | 7: pooled tokens feasible; leakage and serialization risks |

At 40% progress, select the **audited cutoff comparison**. It explicitly targets older interests competing with recent preferences and broad associations displacing specific present choices. Context-specific supervision may address Industrial/Electronics weak-margin tails; neither user benefit nor diagnostic improvement is established.

Verify the uniform control, then change only conditional nonterminal probabilities: endpoint probability remains 0.1; remaining mass equally mixes uniform eligible positions and their latest ten. Preserve separately normalized half-weight losses, strict-prefix MASK inputs, one BERT4Rec/checkpoint per category, and fixed host macro HR@10.

Persist actual counts and checkpoint counters; repair contradictory definitions. Inspect context-length, popularity and repetition shifts as possible shortcuts. Revisit the same twenty users for specific-choice and staleness judgments. The reported 0.5850 differs from snapshot macro 0.58125; provenance remains unresolved. Paired bootstrap intervals, if outcomes exist, describe fixed-model validation-user variability, excluding adaptive selection uncertainty [6,7]. Sampled HR@10 does not establish full-catalog superiority [8].

idea.description: Complete an audited, endpoint-preserving recent-cutoff comparison against the supplied uniform-cutoff BERT4Rec control. Preserve one independently trained model per category and change only the conditional distribution of nonterminal terminal-mask targets. Describe this as a controlled BERT4Rec sampling adaptation: terminal-mask training is explicit in original BERT4Rec, recency-biased target selection is established by RSS, and strict-prefix target construction distinguishes this experiment from RSS.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale interests competing with recent preferences and broad thematic associations displacing specific current choices. Recent strict-prefix supervision could improve both through more relevant target exposure, although this remains a hypothesis and cannot establish equipment compatibility, unsatisfied needs or purchase intent. Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have measured weak-margin rates of 0.1093 and 0.1025, respectively, motivating context-specific discrimination checks. Their positive tenth-percentile margins, 0.3545 and 0.4825, supersede the negative margins reported in earlier inspirations; those earlier values must not be presented as the current diagnosis. Existing recent10 snapshots and the reported 0.5850 do not establish a matched improvement over a verified control. Equal-count snapshots also contradict Bernoulli(0.75) definitions, requiring an instrumentation correction before interpreting allocation effects. At 40% progress, resolving this comparison is more interpretable than simultaneously adding time attention, text features or negative mining.
idea.implementation_notes:
Use the supplied corrected BERT4Rec and verify the supplied uniform control before allocating another training trial. Do not inspect other trial directories or reuse their trained checkpoints. Verify through host-supplied configuration, execution records and outcomes rather than assuming repeated inspirations describe independent evidence. If a verifiable matched control is unavailable, describe the comparison as incomplete. A newly authorized control would be a separate budgeted trial, never an additional predictor within the treatment. Each executed trial trains exactly one independent model for each of Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl; deployment loads one selected checkpoint per category without averaging, independent experts or score fusion.

Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], fixed splits, single-GPU execution, trial-local artifacts, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per executed epoch. Resolve epochs as min(200, int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200'))) and reject nonpositive values. All executed controls, treatments, diagnostics, debugging and failures consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. LLM time and final held-out inference remain separately recorded by the host. Record versions, hardware, determinism settings, resolved hyperparameters, evaluated configurations and actual elapsed GPU time.

Preserve the supplied control's architecture and optimization: maxlen=128, hidden_units=64, num_blocks=2, num_heads=2, dropout=0.2, Adam lr=0.001, weight_decay=0.0, gradient_clip=5.0 and total batch_size=128. Preserve validation every five epochs, patience of twenty epochs since the earliest best checkpoint checked at validation, and earliest-maximum category validation HR@10 checkpoint selection. Keep the same schedule and stopping rule in both arms. Category-specific checkpoint selection remains the supplied protocol; compare complete four-category configurations by host macro HR@10 rather than creating an unplanned category-wise winner combination across configurations.

The supplied snapshots specify 64 independently sampled eligible users per branch, with replacement, latest-maxlen reconstruction with 0.15 MASK-only corruption and one-target fallback, and terminal contexts of at most maxlen-1 preceding events. Preserve these choices and the baseline fallback implementation exactly. If its details are not present in supplied code, record the ambiguity rather than inventing a replacement while claiming a cutoff-only comparison. Use L=0.5*CE_reconstruction_sum/N_reconstruction+0.5*CE_terminal_sum/N_terminal, with both counts positive. The denominators are valid target counts, not example counts. Preserve the real-item-only full-softmax denominator over IDs 1..itemnum, tied item_emb.weight[1:itemnum+1], ID-minus-one labels, no output bias and branch-specific sum-then-divide reduction. PAD and MASK are excluded from the denominator by explicit slicing. Preserve repeated occurrences and their targets. Do not add negative mining, exclude historical items from this denominator, change endpoint probability, replace equal branch counts with Bernoulli allocation or alter objective normalization.

For histories of length n>2, the terminal endpoint has probability 0.1. Conditional nonterminal control probabilities are uniform over zero-based positions 1..n-2. Treatment probabilities mix that uniform distribution equally with uniform selection from its latest min(10,n-2) positions. Thus unconditional treatment probability for a nonterminal position t is 0.9*(0.5/(n-2)+0.5/min(10,n-2)*I[t>=n-1-min(10,n-2)]). Histories shorter than two events are ineligible and counted; length-two histories select their sole eligible endpoint with probability one and are recorded as exceptions. The arms coincide for n<=12. The 0.1 endpoint probability concerns only terminal-branch selection; reconstruction can additionally supervise the final event. The treatment changes event-position recency, not elapsed-time decay.

Retain SeedSequence([42, category_id, one_based_epoch, zero_based_batch, purpose_id]) streams, category IDs 0..3 in the stated order, purpose IDs users=0, cutoffs=1, masks=2, negatives=3, and reconstruction-then-terminal user draw order. Match user draws and cutoff uniforms across arms where host execution permits; apply each policy's inverse CDF to the same cutoff uniform. Keep model initialization/dropout RNG separate from data RNG. The negative stream is for compatible diagnostic sampling, not the full-softmax training loss. If data workers are used, preserve their seeding and dedicated generator. These streams change original cold-start random draws; shared uniforms do not guarantee identical realized targets, masks or hardware-level determinism. A control differing in these streams is not a verified cutoff-only control.

Terminal inputs contain only occurrences before the selected target followed by reserved MASK. Exclude the selected occurrence and every subsequent event, retaining earlier occurrences of the same item. Reconstruction uses genuinely masked labels without shifted-target leakage. Require maxlen>=2. All sequences remain left padded; use the maximum nonpadding index for readout, never nonpadding_count-1. Inference appends MASK after truncating to the latest maxlen-1 history events. This sampler-only treatment needs no architectural inference change: retain the corrected embedded predictor writer and ensure working/predict.py uses identical model definitions, checkpoint keys, special-token conventions, truncation and category routing. Each category must load exactly one independently trained checkpoint.

Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), actual view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data interfaces. The loader continues yielding (None, sequence, positive, negative), with tensors B x L. Preserve family-specific sample_batch behavior. Correct branch-allocation definitions only after confirming executed training; the supplied snapshots indicate fixed equal-count branches, not Bernoulli(0.75). If records cannot resolve the discrepancy, label allocation uncertain rather than declaring it repaired. Definitions must be derived from the resolved protocol and measured metrics, not copied from a different proposal.

Persist selected-checkpoint counters explicitly alongside the state dictionary and restore the matching snapshot for diagnosis. Report branch examples, valid targets, actual detached CE sums, denominators, objective contributions, coefficient masses, endpoint/singleton/ineligible counts, expected and realized cutoffs, long-history exposure, target-item counts, training item frequencies, context-length histograms, timing and validation evaluation counts. Coefficient mass is neither loss-value share nor gradient share. Global target-weighted CE differs from averaging batch objectives. Unmatched probe bookkeeping remains unavailable; do not reconstruct branch allocation from final-position coverage, since both branches can supervise a sequence's final position. RankMe concentration and directional alignment are not proof of collapse, recommendation diversity or user-facing failures.

Track intervention coverage accurately. The approximately 16–28% long-history user fractions describe eligibility for differing distributions, not the fraction of targets that changed. Endpoint draws are unchanged, and matched inverse-CDF draws can choose identical nonterminal positions. Record long-history nonterminal draws and, when available from deterministic policy calculations, the fraction of matched draws selecting different targets. Do not claim that the intervention affects every terminal example from a long history.

Select using the unchanged host macro validation HR@10: 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negative candidates and evaluation seed 42. The snapshot category scores 0.630, 0.605, 0.445 and 0.645 average to 0.58125, whereas inspirations report 0.5850. Keep their provenance separate until reconciled. One additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. Do not infer a treatment effect, confidence interval or independent replication from these aggregate scores.

If host-provided aligned per-user binary outcomes are available, pair by category and user, report gained/lost hits, and bootstrap 200 users with replacement independently within each category for 10,000 replicates using analysis seed 42. Apply identical resampling indices to both arms and equally average category differences. Report observed difference and percentile 95% interval. Otherwise omit the interval. Appropriate interpretation: paired bootstrap intervals describe validation-user resampling variability for fixed selected models and fixed candidate sets; they exclude training randomness and checkpoint/configuration selection uncertainty. They do not correct winner's optimism or guarantee nominal post-selection coverage. Population interpretation additionally requires approximately independent, representative users. Do not introduce new splits or alter the evaluator to address these limitations. Test files and labels remain inaccessible during search; the host alone performs the final held-out evaluation.

HR@10 against 99 sampled negatives evaluates the pinned sampled-candidate task. Published sampled-metric research shows that full-catalog model ordering can differ; a narrow bootstrap interval cannot establish full-catalog superiority. For qualitative follow-up, use the same twenty real training users, five/category, and full-catalog unseen-item recommendations from each category's sole model. Track concrete willingness-to-choose rationales tied to recent behavior, staleness, lower-ranked specific matches, duplicate capabilities, incompatible specifications, excessive scale and absent current tasks. Separate uncertain suitability from rejection and distinguish qualitative evidence from sampled validation HR@10.

Only public histories, item titles/descriptions and observed timestamps are available. Generic metadata examples do not authorize ratings, reviews, categories, prices or stores; simulator diversity/conformity traits remain unobserved. Text and time are future directions, not additions to this treatment. Temporal attention would need unknown MASK time or anchoring to the last observed event, never the target timestamp. A future text encoder must be randomly initialized, jointly trained within the one network, and mask target ID and text together.

Inspect target-frequency, repetition and context-length shifts for shortcuts. Recency sampling may improve validation through popular targets, longer contexts, repeated purchases or alignment with the chronological validation endpoint rather than better inference of current need. These are possible mechanisms, not established explanations. The primary comparison estimates the total sampling-policy effect and cannot isolate these mediators. Later budgeted context-matched, temporal or semantic ablations must be separate experiments with explicitly changed eligibility or architecture. Repeated proposals and repeated 0.5850 entries are not independent evidence. Describe small selected gains as provisional and make no claim that this method resolves compatibility or already-satisfied needs.
idea.pseudocode:
import numpy as np

CATEGORIES = ('Movies_and_TV', 'Industrial_and_Scientific',
              'Electronics', 'CDs_and_Vinyl')


def data_rng(category_id, epoch, batch_id, purpose_id):
    # epoch is one-based; batch_id is zero-based.
    return np.random.default_rng(np.random.SeedSequence(
        [42, category_id, epoch, batch_id, purpose_id]))


def choose_target(history, u, treatment=True):
    """Return zero-based target occurrence and status from one uniform."""
    if not 0.0 <= u < 1.0:
        raise ValueError('u must be in [0, 1)')
    n = len(history)
    if n < 2:
        raise ValueError('Terminal histories require preceding context')
    if n == 2:
        return 1, 'singleton_endpoint_exception'
    if u < 0.1:
        return n - 1, 'endpoint'
    m = n - 2  # Eligible nonterminal indices are 1..n-2.
    probabilities = np.full(m, 1.0 / m)
    if treatment:
        k = min(10, m)
        probabilities *= 0.5
        probabilities[-k:] += 0.5 / k
    cdf = np.cumsum(probabilities)
    cdf[-1] = 1.0
    v = (u - 0.1) / 0.9
    t = min(int(np.searchsorted(cdf, v, side='right')), m - 1) + 1
    return t, 'nonterminal'


def terminal_example(history, u, maxlen, mask_id, treatment=True):
    if maxlen < 2:
        raise ValueError('maxlen must allow context and MASK')
    t, status = choose_target(history, u, treatment)
    context = list(history[max(0, t - maxlen + 1):t])
    sequence = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
    tokens = context + [mask_id]
    sequence[-len(tokens):] = tokens
    return sequence, int(history[t]), status


def final_nonpadding_indices(sequence):
    # NumPy equivalent of the required torch maximum-position readout.
    positions = np.arange(sequence.shape[1])[None, :]
    indices = np.where(sequence != 0, positions, -1).max(axis=1)
    if np.any(indices < 0):
        raise ValueError('Readout requires a nonempty sequence')
    return indices


# Integration into the supplied corrected control, not a standalone train.py.
# Preserve its model, preprocessing, predictor writer and helper implementations.
# For each category, epoch=1..resolved_epochs, batch_id=0..199:
#   user_rng = data_rng(category_id, epoch, batch_id, 0)
#   cutoff_rng = data_rng(category_id, epoch, batch_id, 1)
#   mask_rng = data_rng(category_id, epoch, batch_id, 2)
#   negative_rng = data_rng(category_id, epoch, batch_id, 3)
#   reconstruction_users = sample_64_eligible_users(user_rng)
#   terminal_users = sample_64_eligible_users(user_rng)
#   reconstruction = baseline_masked_reconstruction(reconstruction_users, mask_rng)
#   uniforms = cutoff_rng.random(64)
#   terminal = [terminal_example(h, u, maxlen, MASK, treatment=True)
#               for h, u in zip(histories(terminal_users), uniforms)]
#   reconstruction_sum, Nr = baseline_real_item_ce_sum(model, reconstruction)
#   terminal_sum, Nt = baseline_real_item_ce_sum(model, terminal)
#   assert Nr > 0 and Nt == 64
#   loss = 0.5 * reconstruction_sum / Nr + 0.5 * terminal_sum / Nt
#   baseline_optimizer_step(loss)
#   persist_actual_counts_losses_cutoffs_context_lengths_and_timing()
#   # Audit policy overlap without another model or altered training RNG:
#   # compare choose_target(h, u, True) and choose_target(h, u, False).
# Use treatment=False only in a separate authorized matched-control trial.
# Save one selected checkpoint/category plus its matching measured counters.
# Keep the supplied predictor writer; each category loads one checkpoint.
# Inference input: left_pad(history[-(maxlen-1):] + [MASK], maxlen).
# Read the maximum nonpadding position, never nonpadding_count - 1.
# Diagnose through the existing ModelView and family-specific sample_batch.
# Make definitions describe verified execution; unresolved conflicts stay explicit.


def paired_validation_bootstrap(hits_control, hits_treatment):
    """Only use aligned binary arrays supplied by the host evaluator."""
    differences = []
    for category in CATEGORIES:
        control = np.asarray(hits_control[category], dtype=np.float64)
        treatment = np.asarray(hits_treatment[category], dtype=np.float64)
        if control.shape != (200,) or treatment.shape != (200,):
            raise ValueError('Require 200 aligned users per category')
        if not (np.isin(control, [0, 1]).all()
                and np.isin(treatment, [0, 1]).all()):
            raise ValueError('Require binary hit indicators')
        differences.append(treatment - control)
    observed = float(np.mean([d.mean() for d in differences]))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
    replicates = np.empty(10000)
    for r in range(10000):
        category_deltas = []
        for d in differences:
            indices = rng.integers(0, 200, size=200)
            category_deltas.append(d[indices].mean())
        replicates[r] = np.mean(category_deltas)
    interval = np.percentile(replicates, [2.5, 97.5])
    gained = {c: int((d > 0).sum()) for c, d in zip(CATEGORIES, differences)}
    lost = {c: int((d < 0).sum()) for c, d in zip(CATEGORIES, differences)}
    return observed, interval, gained, lost

# Bootstrap interpretation: fixed selected models and fixed candidates;
# excludes retraining, candidate-draw and adaptive-selection uncertainty.
# Never reconstruct user hits from aggregate HR or change the host evaluator.

originality.positive: The fixed endpoint probability, strict-prefix context and isolated conditional nonterminal distribution define a precise controlled adaptation distinct from RSS's retained-future-context set prediction.
originality.negative: BERT4Rec explicitly includes final-item-only training, and RSS establishes recency-biased target selection. Neither terminal masking nor recency sampling is new; novelty lies mainly in experimental specification.

future_potential.positive: A verified comparison can determine whether target exposure merits later temporal or semantic modeling while testing stale-interest and broad-association failures.
future_potential.negative: Different probabilities apply only to histories longer than twelve events, and policy effects mix target exposure with context length and repetition. Sampled validation gains may not transfer to full-catalog choices, compatibility or unsatisfied needs.

code_difficulty.positive: The atomic sampler change preserves the BERT4Rec backbone, checkpoint architecture and inference computation.
code_difficulty.negative: The full reproducible experiment requires verified control provenance, matched RNG streams, checkpoint-specific counters, exact normalization and repaired diagnostic definitions. A rating of three understates this audit and integration work.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Section 3.6 explicitly describes random masked-item reconstruction and additional training examples masking only the final item.
Inference appends a reserved MASK and predicts from its representation.
Provides the required bidirectional backbone and establishes terminal-mask supervision as prior work.
limitations: Does not establish randomly choosing arbitrary historical prefix endpoints and removing all subsequent context as its training augmentation policy.
Discusses exhaustive prefix–next-item examples as computationally expensive; combinatorial Cloze expansion concerns masking patterns.
Does not specify the proposed fixed endpoint probability, conditional recent-ten mixture or performance on the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: Effective and Efficient Training for Sequential Recommendation using Recency Sampling
contributions: Petrov and Macdonald's RecSys 2022 paper establishes RSS; DOI: 10.1145/3523227.3546785. A later journal expansion adds the RSS prefix to its title.
Samples c=max(1,floor(n*tau)) target positions with replacement using p(k) proportional to alpha^(n-k), establishing recency-biased target selection without an explicit recency-weighted loss.
Removes sampled target positions and predicts a set of positives from the remaining sequence, including events after an interior target; experiments use BCE and LambdaRank.
For 0<alpha<1, the newest per-draw probability is (1-alpha)/(1-alpha^n), and a position's inclusion probability is 1-(1-p(k))^c; alpha=1 gives uniform draws.
limitations: Does not implement the proposed strict-prefix positional-MASK supervision or fixed endpoint probability.
Its retained subsequent context and set-prediction objective prevent treating its results as direct evidence for this BERT4Rec adaptation.
Directly limits originality claims for recency-based target selection.

related_work.title: Sequential Masked Modeling
contributions: The supplied search summary reports investigation of sliding windows and penultimate-token masking.
Motivates examining supervision and window alignment before adding architectural complexity.
limitations: The supplied findings do not verify the proposed endpoint-preserving nonterminal cutoff mixture under the pinned RecHarness protocol.
Treat the summary as motivation rather than proof of a matched implementation or benchmark improvement.

related_work.title: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Models absolute positions and pairwise elapsed-time relations.
Provides a temporal-attention precedent for a later, separate adaptation inside bidirectional BERT4Rec.
limitations: Its backbone must not replace the required BERT4Rec family.
Purchase intervals do not directly reveal engagement, compatibility or unsatisfied current needs.
Any MASK temporal feature must avoid the unavailable next-event timestamp.

related_work.title: ITS-Rec (2025), as summarized in the supplied search results
contributions: The supplied summary describes incorporating textual item representations into sequential recommendation.
Motivates a future randomly initialized, jointly trained title/description encoder within one model.
limitations: The supplied summary attributes substantial gains to reviews, which are unavailable here.
Does not establish the proposed from-scratch, titles-and-descriptions-only BERT4Rec variant.
Textual similarity cannot establish compatibility, complementarity or specific qualities absent from the supplied descriptions.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling that preserves correspondence between observations across compared arrays.
Supports resampling each user's control and treatment outcomes together within each category.
limitations: Does not itself specify this experiment's equal-category macro aggregation or percentile interval implementation.
Paired user resampling does not measure training, candidate-generation or adaptive-selection uncertainty.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Cawley and Talbot (2010) explain optimism from optimizing noisy finite-sample model-selection criteria.
Supports qualifying intervals computed after checkpoint and configuration selection on the same validation users.
limitations: Does not supply a task-specific correction for this fixed RecHarness protocol.
Freezing selected models before bootstrapping does not remove the preceding selection bias.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Krichene and Rendle (2020) show that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics, including model orderings.
Supports restricting conclusions to the pinned 100-candidate HR@10 task.
limitations: Does not establish whether a particular observed ordering reverses on these four datasets.
Does not justify changing the host evaluator or claiming full-catalog superiority from bootstrap precision.
